periods.analysis: Council should read 2024-Q3 as a red baseline, not a surprise failure: the Rent-Burdened Household Rate is 59.5% against a target of <=45%, the Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count is 2100 against <=2000, and Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target is 82% against >=100%. The affordability gap is showing up most sharply along the airport-seaport job corridor and the Route 7 frequent-service spine, where new leases are moving faster than wage growth for service and logistics workers. The unsheltered count is yellow but already 100 people above target, with outreach teams reporting heavier evening contacts at Pier 3, Eastbank Transit Center, and the North Harbor viaduct. The 82% delivery result reflects real production, but the Harbor Landing and Sandpiper Court inspections both slipped into the next reporting cycle, which matters because timing is now driving the score as much as financing.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Q4 reporting cutoff tight: Planning, Housing, and Inspections should reconcile permit, certificate-of-occupancy, and funding data every Friday by noon so the council packet is defensible. Move Harbor Landing, Sandpiper Court, and the 12 scattered-site rehab permits onto a named Affordable Housing Pipeline Renewal list with weekly issue owners. Add two evening outreach rotations on the Route 7 and Eastbank Transit Center circuit and connect those contacts directly to diversion funds before winter demand rises.

periods.analysis: The red condition deepened in 2024-Q4: Rent-Burdened Household Rate moved from 59.5% to 60.0%, up 0.5 percentage points quarter over quarter. The Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count increased from 2100 to 2180, up 80 people, while Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target fell from 82% to 78%, down 4 percentage points. This is the pattern we were trying to avoid heading into winter: higher rents, more visible homelessness, and fewer units closing before year-end. The main operational drag was not lack of effort; it was sequencing, with fire-life-safety rechecks at Harbor Landing and a delayed transformer release from BayGrid Utilities holding back certificates of occupancy.
periods.recommendations: For Q1, run a Monday 9 a.m. Pipeline Renewal huddle with Housing, Permitting, Fire Marshal, BayGrid, and the two delayed developers until each blocked unit has a dated action. Authorize the winter hotel block extension near Harborview Station for families already matched to case managers, with exits tracked by name rather than aggregate bed counts. Give council a one-page variance note showing the +0.5 percentage-point rent-burden movement, +80 unsheltered movement, and -4 percentage-point unit-delivery movement so departments can explain the work clearly and consistently.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q1 remained red and moved in the wrong direction again: Rent-Burdened Household Rate increased from 60.0% to 60.4%, up 0.4 percentage points. The Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count rose from 2180 to 2240, up 60 people, and Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target dropped from 78% to 73%, down 5 percentage points and now red. The quarter was affected by post-holiday eviction filings, slower LIHTC draw approvals, and weather delays on the Mariner Lofts podium pour. I want us to be candid but fair: the teams are working, but the pipeline is not yet moving at the speed the metric requires.
periods.recommendations: Shift Affordable Housing Pipeline Renewal into a 90-day recovery protocol: every project more than 30 days behind schedule gets a blocker, owner, due date, and Friday status color. Expand shallow rent assistance through the Harbor Stabilization Fund for households on the airport and seaport employment verification lists, because preventing one displacement is faster than rehousing one new unsheltered resident. Ask Legal and Procurement to pre-clear the modular inspection vendor pool by the next council cycle so Mariner Lofts and the scattered-site rehabs do not wait on sequential reviews.

periods.analysis: In 2025-Q2, the overall status stayed red, but the story became more mixed and therefore more manageable. Rent-Burdened Household Rate moved from 60.4% to 60.8%, up 0.4 percentage points, and the Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count moved from 2240 to 2300, up 60 people. Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target improved from 73% to 78%, up 5 percentage points, returning that measure to yellow after the Q1 red result. That improvement came from certificates of occupancy at Harbor Landing Building B and the first 41 units at Sandpiper Court, which tells us the Pipeline Renewal cadence is helping but not yet enough to overcome rent pressure and homelessness inflow.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly Pipeline Renewal huddle and add a second track for utility releases, because BayGrid and Harbor Water signoffs are now the most common last-mile delays. Direct outreach teams to prioritize the Eastbank, Pier 3, and Airport Way cohorts for housing navigation, with a two-week report-back on accepted placements versus declined offers. Bring council a Q2-to-Q3 risk memo that names the +0.4 percentage-point rent-burden increase, +60 unsheltered increase, and +5 percentage-point delivery improvement so the narrative stays balanced and action-oriented.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q3 is the quarter where the red rating became more urgent: Rent-Burdened Household Rate rose from 60.8% to 61.1%, up 0.3 percentage points, and the Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count increased from 2300 to 2360, up 60 people and now red. Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target improved from 78% to 86%, up 8 percentage points, which is meaningful progress but not enough to offset the worsening homelessness and rent-burden measures. The permitting team closed a strong batch at Mariner Lofts and the Alder & 5th rehab cluster, and I want that work recognized. The concern is that summer rent resets and encampment inflow along the freight rail spur are outpacing the housing placements we are generating.
periods.recommendations: Keep the delivery push going: do not pull staff off Pipeline Renewal just because unit delivery improved to 86%; instead, protect the inspection surge through the end of Q4. Stand up a 30/60/90-day unsheltered action plan for the freight rail spur, Pier 3, and Eastbank Transit Center, with named outreach leads and weekly placement targets. Prepare a council budget amendment for flexible landlord incentives tied to Route 7 and Airport Way units, because the rent-burden trend is still red even as production improves.

periods.analysis: 2025-Q4 stayed red, with all three quarter-over-quarter signals reminding us that production gains are fragile. Rent-Burdened Household Rate increased from 61.1% to 61.4%, up 0.3 percentage points, while the Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count rose from 2360 to 2410, up 50 people. Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target fell from 86% to 78%, down 8 percentage points, as the North Quay family housing project missed its elevator inspection window and the Harborview Homes preservation closing moved past year-end. The unsheltered increase slowed slightly from the prior quarter, but at 2410 against a target of <=2000, this remains a concerned-but-managed red result.
periods.recommendations: Put North Quay and Harborview Homes back on the top of the Pipeline Renewal agenda with elevator, title, and subsidy-contract owners named before the next council briefing. Lock winter operations now: extend the Harborview Station hotel block, add overnight warming capacity at the Southside Community Center, and publish weekly exits to permanent housing. For the Q1 council packet, separate controllable delivery delays from market rent pressure so departments look accountable without being blamed for factors they do not control.

periods.analysis: 2026-Q1 remained red and, candidly, the trend is still not where we need it: Rent-Burdened Household Rate rose from 61.4% to 61.7%, up 0.3 percentage points. The Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count increased from 2410 to 2450, up 40 people, and Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target declined from 78% to 73%, down 5 percentage points and back to red. The smaller unsheltered increase suggests winter diversion and hotel operations prevented a sharper spike, but the absolute level is still 450 people above target. Unit delivery was pulled down by delayed state reimbursement on the Harborview Homes preservation closing and rework on the North Quay elevator shaft fireproofing.
periods.recommendations: Treat Q2 as a red recovery quarter: Pipeline Renewal should publish a dated closeout plan for Harborview Homes, North Quay, and the remaining Alder & 5th rehab units by the first Friday of the quarter. Continue the hotel and warming-center exit work, but require case conferencing twice weekly for the 75 longest-staying households so shelter does not become the endpoint. Ask Finance to model a bridge-loan reserve for preservation projects awaiting reimbursement, because the 73% delivery result shows cash timing is becoming a performance risk.

periods.analysis: 2026-Q2 is still red, but there are early signs the recovery work is taking hold on delivery. Rent-Burdened Household Rate moved from 61.7% to 61.9%, up 0.2 percentage points, the smallest quarterly increase in this series but still far above the <=45% target. The Point-in-Time Unsheltered Count increased from 2450 to 2487, up 37 people, while Affordable Units Delivered vs Annual Target improved from 73% to 79%, up 6 percentage points and back to yellow. The improvement came from the Harborview Homes preservation close and North Quay partial occupancy, but the homelessness count at 2487 confirms we should not declare victory to council.
periods.recommendations: Sustain Pipeline Renewal through Q3 and add a preservation-only lane so completed financing and inspections translate into occupied units faster. Expand prevention and landlord incentive dollars in the neighborhoods feeding the largest rent-burden increases, especially Airport Way, Eastbank, and South Harbor, with monthly lease-up reporting. For the next council update, frame Q2 as managed red: acknowledge the +0.2 percentage-point rent-burden movement and +37 unsheltered movement, then show the +6 percentage-point delivery gain and the specific projects scheduled to close next.

periods.analysis: Affordable unit delivery remains above its annual target, but rent burden rose to 52.3% and the unsheltered component rose to 1,276. Trust-fund loan closings have slipped; awards should not be counted as occupied homes.
periods.recommendations: Resolve closing dependencies, track placements and preservation, and report the unfavorable household outcomes beside delivered units.
